## What this tool is for

`capability:launch-agent` puts an agent on work in the three cases a **plan-fleet
launch cannot express**:

| You want | Call |
|---|---|
| An agent on an **ad-hoc brief** (no plan, no fleet ceremony) | `capability:launch-agent { brief }` |
| A **dead** agent back, mid-thread, with its context intact | `capability:launch-agent { resume: { agentId }, brief }` |
| To **branch** a live agent's thread without disturbing it | `capability:launch-agent { resume: { agentId }, fork: true, brief }` |

It is NOT a replacement for `fleet:launch-on-plan` — that stays the right tool for
"open N members and work this plan". The routing rule:

> **Work is a plan** → `fleet:launch-on-plan`. **Work is a brief, or the agent
> already exists** → `capability:launch-agent`. **Headless, no desktop window** →
> `fleet:launch-on-plan { headless: true }` (see
> [desktop-fleet-vs-loop-cup](/internal/docs/agent-insights/desktop-fleet-vs-loop-cup)).

:::note[This row used to say `cup:spawn` — it no longer works]
The "headless background grinder on ranked work" route was `cup:spawn` (a Mug-supervised
nursery cup). The Mug · Kettle · Cup tier was **retired 2026-08-09** and `cup:spawn` /
`fleet:place_batch` **refuse**. A headless FLEET is not a cup: it is leader-led su members
with no desktop window, so `fleet:launch-on-plan { headless: true }` is the replacement.
See [the Mug · Kettle · Cup tier is retired](/internal/docs/agent-insights/mug-kettle-cup-tier-is-retired).
:::

All three sit on ONE shared core (`agent-launch-core.ts`) — command construction,
fleet/launched-by/account injection, resume resolution. There is deliberately no
second spawn path to drift out of sync.

## Trap 1: a scripted resume that does not pin an account stops on the login picker

This is the owner-visible bug that motivated the whole thing — *"why is it asking
me to log in?"*

`psu`'s `resumeAccountPlan` shows an **interactive account picker** when a resume
carries neither `--account` nor `--no-picker`. A human typing `psu --resume` picks
an account and moves on. A *scripted* launch has nobody to pick, so the agent sits
on a login prompt forever, looking hung.

Both `capability:launch-agent` and `capability:terminal` now inject
`--account=default` into any `--resume` command that lacks one, and
`buildAgentLaunchCommand` always emits `--no-picker --account=<acct>`. **If you
construct a psu resume command by hand anywhere else, pin the account yourself.**

On **macOS the default is `--account=auto`**, not `default`: a per-session config
dir cannot reach the Keychain login, so darwin routes through the gateway account
(`defaultLaunchAccount`).

## Trap 2: resuming a LIVE agent is not what you want — fork it

An in-place resume **re-attaches the original coord `ownerId`**. Do that to an
agent that is still alive and you now have two processes answering to one identity:
wakes, claims and messages land in a coin-flip. (This is WI-3882.)

So: `resolveResumeTarget` detects a live source and the tool **auto-forks it**,
with a loud note in the report. A fork gets a **fresh identity** — which is the
other half of the trade:

> A forked agent is a NEW ownerId that nobody — not you, not the fleet — can
> address until it boots and registers presence. You cannot pre-wake it, and you
> cannot hand it work by id in the same turn you launch it.

That is exactly why the brief matters (below).

## How the first turn actually gets delivered

A launched agent that opens IDLE is useless — someone has to give it its first
turn, and the seam differs by mode:

- **Fresh launch** → the brief rides the spawn-safe env var
  `PAPERCUSP_KICKOFF_PROMPT`, and `psu-launcher` turns it into the CLI's positional
  prompt (`kickoffPositionalArgs`, gated on `--no-picker`, suppressed by
  `--no-kickoff`). Free-form text must NOT be passed as `--kickoff=<text>` inside a
  console greeting one-liner — it gets double-quoted and breaks the shell.
- **Resume / fork** → there is no CLI seam at all (`claude --resume <id> "<prompt>"`
  is not a supported form, and a fork's fresh ownerId is unaddressable from
  outside). Instead **psu's own managed pty host injects the first turn**: it waits
  for the agent to settle at its prompt, writes the turn, and *verifies submission*
  (`injectTurnAtPrompt` in `psu-pty-host.mjs`). This is the same
  wait-at-prompt + submit-verify machinery the WI-1941 recycle carry-note already
  used — one delivery path, guaranteed or **loudly dropped**, never silently lost.

**Always pass a `brief`.** Without one the agent boots and sits there; the tool
warns you, but a warning is not a turn.

## Cross-backend resume is a port, not a shared native thread

`psu --resume=<tracked Claude row> --agent=codex|omp` uses the session-port
protocol. The distinction matters:

- A same-backend resume reopens the original backend's native transcript.
- A cross-backend port snapshots the source, creates a **new** target session,
  carries history as a managed seed, waits for native persistence, and then lets
  every later resume use the target backend normally.

OMP can appear to resume across models more simply because an OMP thread is
already provider-neutral: OMP owns one conversation representation and sends the
next request to whichever model/provider is selected. That is a good pattern
inside a single host runtime, but it does not make Claude Code JSONL, Codex
rollouts, and OMP thread storage mutually readable. `psu` coordinates those
independent native CLIs, so pretending they share one thread would produce false
lineage and targets that cannot resume natively later.

What the port deliberately copies from OMP's strategy:

- a versioned, provider-independent conversation contract;
- explicit model/provider selection separate from history;
- deterministic history fitting before the target request;
- preserving tool-call/result relationships while normalizing backend syntax.

What it deliberately does not copy:

- relabeling a provider switch as the same native session;
- replaying unbounded history and hoping the target truncates it safely;
- persisting full normalized transcript text in coordination/audit metadata;
- importing source control state, permissions, claims, or prompt authority;
- treating terminal output as proof that the target recorded the seed.

The extra ceremony is the value: inspect is read-only, prepare occurs only after
an egress preview/confirmation, delivery is idempotent, the artifact is one-use,
and `delivered` means the native target transcript contains the managed seed.
Protocol/transform skew and a missing migration fail closed. A stale prepared or
pending port is expired by the existing telemetry-retention routine, which ends
the target, removes the seed, and emits content-free failed-delivery telemetry.

V1 is intentionally narrow: tracked plain Claude sources, Codex/OMP targets, no
native fork combination, and no transfer from an active fleet/loop/claim-bearing
source. That boundary keeps the first implementation auditable while leaving the
contract extensible for future source adapters.

## Trap 3: a launched agent that "never wakes up" is usually not rate-limited

Two failures on this box make a perfectly-launched agent sit at a dead prompt
forever, with **no error anywhere**. Both were found by live-verify on
2026-07-12, and both were misread as "the model hung" / "we got rate limited"
before the real cause turned up. Check these before you blame the API:

**(a) claude's first-run wizard.** Every psu session gets a per-session
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` that **symlinks the global `~/.claude.json` in** — and that
file carries `hasCompletedOnboarding`. If it is ever `false`, claude boots the
first-run **theme picker** instead of a session: the agent never reaches a
prompt, so the kickoff can never land. It also *self-propagates* — the symlink
is write-through, so a session wedged in the wizard writes its
not-yet-onboarded state straight back to the global file and re-arms the trap
for the next launch. `writeInteractiveClaudeConfig` now **asserts** the flag on
every materialize (`ensureOnboardingComplete`), so this self-heals; if you ever
see a launched agent parked on a theme menu, that guard is what failed.

**(b) `--harness` is what makes it a papercusp agent at all.** A fresh launch
without `--harness` boots a *plain* claude: psu skips the su bootstrap, the
per-session config dir is never seeded, and you get (a) as a side effect. The
tool now always harness-scopes a fresh launch. Symptom to recognise: the
session's config dir holds a small *real* `.claude.json` that claude wrote
itself, instead of the ~87-key symlink farm every healthy session has.

## Trap 4: `psu` may not be running the launcher you just edited

`~/.papercusp/bin/psu` is a shim that hardcodes an **absolute path** to one
`psu-launcher.mjs`, and **every operator boot rewrites it to point at that
operator's own tree** — the green operator (`:3070`) stamps in
`papercup-release/…`, the staging operator (`:3170`) stamps in the shared
integration tree. On the dev box both run, so the last boot silently wins.

The consequence is nasty and near-invisible: you edit
`apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs` in the shared tree, launch through
`psu`, and may silently exercise the **release** copy of your file — then
conclude your code does not work. (That is precisely what happened while
verifying the resume/fork kickoff seam: the same command dropped its kickoff at
20:08 and delivered it at 20:19, with no code change in between.) Note this also
punches a hole in the "guaranteed or loudly dropped" promise above — a launcher
that *predates* the seam cannot warn about a kickoff it has never heard of.

To test a launcher change, **bypass the shim** and run the tree's launcher
directly:

```bash
node apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs --no-picker --account=default …
```

(with the `PAPERCUSP_*` env the console wrapper exports). Tracked as WI-4440.

## No "resume the fleet" verb — and why

There is deliberately no one-shot fleet revival. Any single verb has to *guess*
which dead members to bring back (all of them? only the ones that died this hour?
not the one you killed on purpose yesterday?) and every guess is wrong for someone.

Instead `fleet:status` hands the leader the **facts**, per ended member:

- `endedAt` — when it died
- `resumable` / `resumableSessionId` — whether a native session actually exists
- `resumeHint` — when it does not (an omp thread, or a row predating native-id
  tracking → launch that lane fresh instead)

The leader then composes the revival *per member* — resume, fork, or fresh.

## Odds and ends

- **Idempotency.** Pass `idempotencyKey` and a retry/duplicate call returns
  "Already launched (deduped)" instead of spawning a second agent
  (`agent_launch_idempotency`, migration 586). A PG failure never blocks a launch —
  it warns and launches unguarded.
- **Shell safety.** `buildAgentLaunchCommand` *validates* rather than quotes: every
  value must match `/^[A-Za-z0-9._:=@/,+-]+$/` or it throws. Free-form text (the
  brief) never goes on the command line at all — it rides the env.
- **Headless.** `headless: true` launches with no window. Note EI-9748: headless
  children are reaped by the service cgroup on a `:3170` restart.
- **Fleet.** An explicit `fleet` wins; otherwise the launch inherits the *caller's*
  fleet (WI-4234), so a leader's ad-hoc launches join its own fleet by default.
